learning_outcomes.text: Students can systematically integrate sustainability aspects and product life cycles into the development process by capturing legal, functional, and ecological requirements and evaluating them using suitable methods to design robust, economical, and resource-efficient product solutions.

Students can compare materials and manufacturing processes for light and strong components by analyzing properties and failure mechanisms of fiber composite structures to design weight-optimized and recyclable components.

Students can specifically secure product quality and functionality by applying tolerance analyses, testing standards, and metrological methods to ensure technical reliability throughout the product life cycle.

Students can systematically plan and evaluate experiments for product optimization by applying Design-of-Experiments (DoE) methods to real problems to efficiently support data-based development decisions.

syllabus_topics: Organization of national and international protection systems
Standards and basics of geometric tolerancing
Creation of full factorial experimental designs (linear/quadratic)
Statistical evaluation and interpretation of experimental results
assessment_rules: The form of examination (written or oral) will be determined by the lecturer at the beginning of the course.
